title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the preceding pages of the 1981 'Longue Marche' manuscripts). U is a hyperbolic curve over a field K finitely generated over Q, with smooth compactification X and cusps indexed by I. Ũ is the pro-universal cover, π = π1(U ⊗ K̄) is the geometric fundamental group, Γ = Gal(K̄/K), and E_U → Γ is the extension π1(U) → Gal(K̄/K). A section of E_U → Γ is the same as a continuous action of Γ on Ũ compatible with its action on K̄. X' = \hat{Ũ} is the normalization of X in Ũ, i.e. Ũ together with its pro-cusps.

Conjecture B (previous page): every such action of Γ has exactly one fixed point in X'. The fixed point is either 'at finite distance' (a point of Ũ over a rational point x ∈ U(K)) or 'at infinity' (a pro-cusp, i.e. a section normalizing an inertia subgroup L_i ≅ Ẑ(1)). This is the fixed-point form of the section conjecture, including cuspidal sections.

This page unpacks what uniqueness means.
(a) Fixed point at finite distance, x̃ ∈ Ũ^Γ:
 1) The image of x̃ in U is uniquely determined. This is injectivity of U(K) → {sections}/π-conjugacy, the thesis of §1.
 2) π^Γ = (1). The centralizer in π of the section is trivial, so there are no other fixed points of Ũ over that x. The margin adds that here even π^{Γ^0} = (1).
 3) There is no fixed point at infinity at the same time: no L_i is normalized by Γ. So a section of the first type (rational point) is never of the second type (cuspidal). He says this was proved directly earlier.
(b) Fixed point at infinity:
 - Uniqueness of the image in X means a section cannot normalize two different inertia groups L_i and L_j (i ≠ j). He says this is proved except in the case (g,ν) = (0,3).
 - Uniqueness over a fixed i means the L_i normalized by Γ is unique. This is a weakening of the relation 'L_i = Cen π^{Γ^0}' conjectured earlier, i.e. that the elements of π centralized by Γ^0 form exactly L_i.
Here Γ^0 is most plausibly the kernel of the cyclotomic character (Gal(K̄/K(μ_∞))), which acts trivially on L_i ≅ Ẑ(1). That is why one expects π^{Γ^0} = L_i in the cuspidal case but π^{Γ^0} = 1 in the rational-point case.
The next page strengthens Conjecture B: Γ^0 alone should already have a unique fixed point in X'. That would give π^{Γ^0} = (1), resp. π^{Γ^0} ⊂ Norm_π(L_i) = L_i.

Purpose: to break the section conjecture (with cusps) into separately checkable statements: injectivity, trivial centralizers, disjointness of rational and cuspidal sections, uniqueness of the cusp, and a centralizer = inertia relation.
errors: The (0,3) exception is honestly flagged as not established. In fact, for the tripod over a number field, a section normalizing two distinct cuspidal inertia groups is also excluded by later work (e.g. via Nakamura's results on centralizers and normalizers of inertia, and Stix's treatment of cuspidal sections), so the gap closes.

The relation 'L_i = Cen π^{Γ^0}' as written is ambiguous. Read literally as the centralizer of π^{Γ^0} it would be odd. The next page makes clear the intended statement is π^{Γ^0} = L_i, i.e. the centralizer of Γ^0 in π equals L_i.

ideas.what: The section conjecture phrased as: any continuous Galois action on the pro-universal cover, compatible with the action on K̄, has exactly one fixed point in the normalized compactification X' (cusps included).
ideas.modern_name: Section conjecture including cuspidal sections (fixed-point / 'packets' formulation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983); cuspidal refinement worked out by Nakamura, Stix, Hoshi, Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983), in Geometric Galois Actions vol. 1 (1997); the fixed-point formulation is in the Longue Marche manuscripts

ideas.what: Injectivity of the section map from U(K) to conjugacy classes of sections.
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity part of the section conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (via Mordell–Weil / Kummer theory); Nakamura; Stix

ideas.what: Trivial centralizer of a section in π (π^Γ = 1), and even π^{Γ^0} = 1 for sections coming from rational points.
A section coming from a rational point is not cuspidal, and a cuspidal section normalizes a unique inertia group L_i (except for an unproved (0,3) case).
ideas.modern_name: Disjointness of cuspidal and non-cuspidal sections; uniqueness of the cusp of a cuspidal section

ideas.what: The relation π^{Γ^0} = L_i, where Γ^0 is likely the kernel of the cyclotomic character.
ideas.modern_name: Centralizer of a cuspidal section equals cuspidal inertia (over K(μ_∞))
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (related to Nakamura's normalizer/centralizer results and Mochizuki's work)

missed.claim: Grothendieck conjectures that for any section, the centralizer in π of the subgroup Γ^0 (plausibly Gal(K̄/K(μ_∞))) is either trivial (rational-point sections) or exactly the cuspidal inertia group L_i (cuspidal sections). He proposes this as a strengthening of the uniqueness part of the section conjecture. As a statement about arbitrary sections, not just geometric ones, it is not clearly settled in the literature.
missed.quote: ce qui est un affaiblissement de la relation L_i = Cen π^{Γ^0} pour ces opérations, conjecturée plus haut.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a group-theoretic criterion that separates cuspidal from non-cuspidal sections using only the cyclotomic-kernel part of Galois. That is relevant to current work on the section conjecture over cyclotomic-type or infinite extensions.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful decomposition of the section conjecture into injectivity, trivial centralizer, cusp/non-cusp disjointness and cusp uniqueness. Grothendieck claims these were proved directly except for the (0,3) case. Most of these statements were later established and credited to Nakamura, Stix and others. The Γ^0-centralizer refinement is a modestly notable unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: '(i.e. il n'y a pas d'autres pts fixes dans Ũ sur ce x ∈ U(K))', meaning above this x.

3°) 'il n'y a pas en même temps de pt fixe x̂ à l'infini — i.e. il n'existe pas de L_i normalisé par Γ, i.e. un scindage du premier type n'est pas en même temps du deuxième (fait que nous avons établi directement, précédemment).'
'l'unicité de l'image dans X signifie que nos actions effectives ne peuvent normaliser à la fois un L_i et un L_j (i≠j)'.
'— dessus d'un i∈I fixé' should read 'au-dessus d'un i ∈ I fixé'.
The margin probably reads: 'c'est un cas particulier de mes "conjectures" ... qu'il faudrait ... ici π^{Γ^0}=(1)'.
